## Why

The statement-enforcement verification pull request (pull request 91, for issue 33) went through eight review rounds. In each one, CodeRabbit found another shell construct that the `testNamePatterns` audit in `test/process-fixture.test.ts` reads differently from a real shell. Patching one construct per round does not converge. The audit needs one strict grammar.

## Class

`testNamePatterns` extracts `--test-name-pattern` values from linked test commands with regular expressions. A shell splits words, expands, substitutes and quotes the command in ways those regular expressions do not model. So the audit can certify a command that selects other tests or no tests.

## Open findings to close as one change

1. An unquoted spaced alternation (`--test-name-pattern=release gate import allows|…`) is read as `release`; the rest of the phrase and the pipe are missed.
2. A substitution directly after a closed quoted pattern (`"a"$(…)` or `"a"` followed by a backtick) is not rejected.
3. Unquoted escaped whitespace (`a\ b`) in a selector is not rejected.
4. The regression command linked in `.agents/pm/history/pm-ado-sdk-adoption.jsonl` is not portable between POSIX shells and cmd.exe.
5. `test/closeout-provenance.test.ts`: the provenance test does not handle a checkout that already has CRLF line endings.
6. `docs/typed-relations.md`: after a failed import, require reconciliation before exporting, and test recovery when the remote parent changed.

## Proposed fix

- Tokenize each linked command with one strict shell-word grammar. A word is either a safe unquoted word or a closed double-quoted word without expansion. Every other construct (single quotes, `$`, backticks, `%VAR%`, escaped whitespace, redirection, pipes or separators adjacent to a pattern) is refused.
- Take the pattern from the token that follows `--test-name-pattern`.
- Back the grammar with must-refuse and must-allow corpora, and give it a revert proof.
- Fix items 5 and 6 separately; each needs its own regression test.

## Acceptance

- All six findings above are covered by the corpora or by their own tests.
- Every current linked test command in `.agents/pm` still passes the audit.
- Reverting the tokenizer fails the corpus test.
Replace the piecemeal linked-test pattern audit with a strict shell-word tokenizer, and close the remaining recovery-doc and CRLF findings
